item.title: Beyond spouting statistics, Peter Obi has nothing to offer — Shettima
item.description: Vice-President Kashim Shettima has criticised the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, saying he has nothing to offer Nigerians beyond what he described as questionable statistics and his opposition to restoring petrol subsidy. Shettima made the remarks at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit, where he acknowledged Obi’s position on subsidy removal but questioned the substance of his economic proposals. “I respect Peter Obi for having the courage to say he’s not going to restore the petrol subsidy, but beyond spouting some dubious statistics, Mr Peter Obi has absolutely nothing to offer,” the Vice-President said. The latest criticism marks another public attack by Shettima on Obi, whom he recently accused of relying on misleading statistics and economic prescriptions that may not suit Nigeria’s circumstances. Shettima recently questioned Obi’s comparisons between Nigeria and Bangladesh, arguing that economic policies cannot be transferred from one country to another without considering their differences. He illustrated his argument with a clothing-size analogy, saying: “He seems convinced that a size 36 shirt tailored for Bangladesh will somehow fit Nigeria’s size 52 frame.” According to Shettima, Nigeria’s economic policies must reflect its population, institutions, political environment and economic structure rather than depend on models developed for other countries. “A country of over 250 million people cannot be governed through borrowed statistics and economic prescriptions detached from its peculiarities,” he added. The Vice-President also challenged Obi’s claim that he won the 2023 presidential election, describing the assertion as unsupported by evidence. Shettima characterised the claim as a “delusion of grandeur” and criticised what he portrayed as an attempt to present old political ideas as a new direction for Nigeria. item.title: After patient’s evacuation, is Nigeria Ebola-free? – WHO clarifies
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Nigeria currently has no confirmed case of Ebola following the medical evacuation of the country’s index patient to Switzerland. But the World Health Organisation, WHO, has not declared the country Ebola-free. Read Also: Nigeria has no Ebola case after patient’s evacuation to Switzerland – WHO The WHO Nigeria office said in a post on X on Monday that public health officials were monitoring people who might have been exposed to the virus. “WHO has not declared Nigeria Ebola‑free. Nigeria currently has no confirmed case of Ebola following the medical evacuation of the index patient to Switzerland. “Health officials are closely monitoring 52 contacts who may have been exposed,” the post reads. “Under the International Health Regulations, a country can only be declared Ebola‑free after a 42‑day countdown following the last confirmed case testing negative twice for the virus or, in this situation, after the evacuation of the confirmed case. “This period is then followed by heightened surveillance.” The clarification came hours after reports were making rounds that Nigeria had been declared Ebola-free. Vanguard earlier reported that Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Ali Pate, on Monday confirmed the departure of the Swiss patient and spouse via an air ambulance to Switzerland. Pate said the patient had improved clinically and was stable, conscious and communicating before the evacuation. He, however, cautioned that her improved condition did not necessarily mean she was no longer infectious. The WHO Regional Director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, said the Nigerian medical team had successfully managed the patient through the acute phase of the illness and stabilised her condition before the evacuation. The NCDC earlier on Sunday said that 53 contacts linked to the case had been identified and followed up. They included health workers, domestic staff and the patient’s husband. Ebola patient evacuated to Switzerland as Nigeria continues monitoring contacts Nigeria’s first confirmed Ebola patient in the current regional outbreak has been medically evacuated from Abuja to Switzerland, following a significant improvement in her condition. Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate confirmed that the patient was stable, conscious, and communicating before departure. Her husband, a Swiss diplomat who has shown no symptoms, accompanied her. The transfer does not mean the patient is no longer infectious. Strict medical precautions remain necessary, and Swiss authorities will assume responsibility for her treatment. Nigeria continues monitoring 52 other contacts. Authorities say there are currently no confirmed Ebola patients remaining in the country, although contact tracing continues. Why it matters: The evacuation changes Nigeria’s immediate case-management responsibilities, but not the need to detect possible secondary infections. The primary source of the patient’s infection also remains unresolved. Watch : Test results among contacts, the outcome of investigations into the patient’s travel history and further updates from the NCDC and Africa CDC. 2. Those identified include Peter Obi, former Senate Presidents Bukola Saraki and David Mark, and former Aviation Minister Stella Oduah. The inquiries concern alleged failures to declare offshore assets or business interests while holding public office. The investigations do not establish wrongdoing. Offshore company ownership is not inherently illegal; the relevant questions concern compliance with asset-declaration and public-office rules. Why it matters : The inquiries concern public-office accountability and include prominent political figures involved in Nigeria’s political landscape. Watch : Formal CCB statements, responses from those named, and whether any investigation leads to proceedings before the Code of Conduct Tribunal. 3. The Nigeria Democratic Congress has announced a 118-member National Campaign Council ahead of the January 2027 elections. Vice-presidential candidate Rabiu Kwankwaso is co-vice-chairman, while Ibrahim Abdulkarim has been named Director-General. The party scheduled the council’s formal inauguration for today in Abuja. item.title: Man Utd consider Howe, Nagelsmann, Conte to replace under-fire Carrick
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United are considering Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte as potential replacements for head coach Michael Carrick, whose future is in serious doubt following the club’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth, sources have told ESPN. According to ESPN, the defeat at Old Trafford on Sunday intensified pressure on Carrick, coming five days after United suffered a 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League. The club have now gone eight games without a win in all competitions and sit 16th in the Premier League, just one point above the relegation zone. ESPN reports that United have begun weighing up alternative managerial options, with former Newcastle United manager Howe and ex-Germany head coach Nagelsmann among the names being considered. Conte, who left Napoli in the summer, would also be open to discussions if United contacted him, the report added. United had reportedly conducted due diligence on several coaches before deciding to appoint Carrick on a two-year contract in May, following his successful interim spell. The former Manchester United midfielder is now facing an uncertain future after failing to secure a response from his players following the heavy defeat to Como. Carrick dropped captain Bruno Fernandes for the Bournemouth game after the midfielder’s criticism of the team’s approach against Como, but United delivered another disappointing performance at Old Trafford. Bournemouth scored three times through Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson, capitalising on defensive errors to deepen United’s crisis. Speaking after the defeat, Carrick said he was unsure what the club would decide about his future. “I totally understand the situation,” he said. “I am not expecting anything, I’m carrying on as normal. I love this place. I’ll always carry on doing what I think is the best for the football club.” United face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, with further difficult fixtures against Aston Villa and Liverpool looming as they seek to arrest their slide. item.title: Atiku pledges gaming support after Lagos Life raises $500,000
item.description: Former vice president and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar has pledged to support Nigeria’s gaming industry following reports that Lagos Life, a Nigerian browser game, raised $500,000 in an angel investment round three days after its developer was incorporated. He made the pledge in a post on X on Monday, saying the game’s early funding success showed the potential of young Nigerian developers to build a globally competitive entertainment industry. “When a game about life in Lagos can raise half a million dollars soon after launch, our young developers are telling us something: the next global entertainment industry can be built right here,” he wrote. Atiku said he would support the sector through e-sports competitions, incentives for gaming infrastructure and financial assistance for local developers. “I will support e-sports leagues and tournaments, offer incentives for gaming infrastructure, and back Nigerian game developers with grants, incubators, and export platforms,” he said. “Our gamers are not wasting time; they are building an industry,” he added. His comments followed a report by TechCabal that Vatar Inc., the company behind Lagos Life, had secured $500,000 in an angel funding round at a valuation of $10m, three days after incorporation. The company’s co-founder and chief executive officer, Shalom Rayhamen, said that the funding round was concluded quickly because of strong investor interest in the game. “We built something people love that is growing very fast, so a lot of investors wanted to be involved,” Rayhamen said. He added, “We got the opportunity to connect and hear their offers, and because we are growing so fast, we closed it quickly so we could focus on the product.” The post Atiku pledges gaming support after Lagos Life raises $500,000 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Over 40 killed in attack on Orthodox Christians in Ethiopia
item.description: At least 43 people have been killed and 18 others wounded in an attack targeting villages, Orthodox Christian churches and homes in Ethiopia’s Oromia region, according to residents and a conflict monitoring organisation. The attack occurred on Saturday in Shirka district, about 270 kilometres south of the Ethiopian capital, Addis Ababa. Residents and the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data project (ACLED) reported the casualties to AFP on Monday, with local accounts suggesting that the death toll could be higher. ACLED said the attack was believed to be religiously motivated and targeted Orthodox Christians, adding that it triggered clashes with local militias that continued through Saturday afternoon and evening. A resident told AFP by telephone that the attack claimed the lives of two family members, while several relatives were reportedly taken hostage in Chole ward of Shirka district. “My sister and uncle were killed, and several of my relatives were taken hostage in Chole ward of Shirka district,” the resident said, requesting anonymity. The resident estimated the death toll at 44, while another local source put the figure at 51. A deacon from one of the affected churches said the killings had left the community devastated and called on the government to restore security. “We are deeply shocked by these tragic killings and are appealing to the government to intervene and restore security,” the deacon said, putting the death toll at 46. He added that some residents had sought refuge in nearby churches following the attack. The state-run Ethiopia Human Rights Commission said it was “following the situation” but did not provide further details. Oromia, Ethiopia’s largest region, has a population of about 40 million and has experienced a prolonged insurgency and tensions among Muslim, Protestant and Orthodox Christian communities. ACLED said attacks against Orthodox Christians in the region had increased since February 2023, with a further escalation reported since last year. It remains unclear whether the latest violence involved the Oromo Liberation Front, the main insurgent group operating in the region. Although political and ethnic representation have been central to the insurgency, religion has also been used to mobilise fighters. Ethiopia continues to grapple with several internal conflicts, including renewed heavy fighting in the northern Tigray region last month. The country’s restrictions on media access have made independent verification of reports from conflict-affected areas difficult. The post Over 40 killed in attack on Orthodox Christians in Ethiopia appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘Immigrants from shithouse country, not welcome,’ Trump blasts Norway over Nobel Peace Prize
item.description: US President Donald Trump attacked Norway during a campaign rally, calling it a “shithouse country,” and said that Norwegian immigrants were not welcome in the United States because its Nobel Committee had not awarded him the Peace Prize. “Frankly, Norway sucks. Norway has become a shithouse country, actually,” he said during Sunday’s speech. Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has made no secret of his desire to win the prestigious Nobel Peace prize. Judge and former UN rights chief Navi Pillay of South Africa was this year’s recipient. Trump has called the committee’s choice “a disgraceful and embarrassing decision” and argued that the award should have gone to him. Trump said Sunday he would welcome immigrants from certain countries but not Norway “because I didn’t get the Nobel Prize.” “So I don’t want anybody from Norway,” he said during the rally in the Michigan town of Port Huron ahead of crucial US midterm elections on November 3. There was no official indication of a new US policy on Norwegian immigrants. Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide responded to Trump’s comments about the Nobel prize on Monday, maintaining that the committee is independent. “He knows very well that the Nobel Committee is independent. We have reminded him of that, in case anyone is wondering – and that is still the case,” he told national broadcaster NRK. Trump came under fire in 2018, during his first term, after using similar vulgar expressions to refer to Haiti and certain African countries. item.title: Nigeria’s NELFUND better than US, UK education loan models – UNIBEN VC
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu, Benin City The Vice Chancellor of the University of Benin, Professor Edoba Omoregie (SAN), on Monday said the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) was the best thing to ever happen to the country’s education system, arguing that the loan scheme is better than the models run by countries like the United States of America and the United Kingdom. Omoregie made this assertion in an interview with Vanguard, but, however, he said he was not impressed by the interest shown so far to access the fund. He said NELFUND was unique in every aspect, including the process of accessing it, the provision of a moratorium before repayment starts, and the percentage to be deducted when the repayment starts, saying that it was almost like a grant for education. He praised President Bola Tinubu for his quick response to the bill by signing the first one passed under President Muhammadu Buhari into law and then immediately repealing it and sending the present one as an executive bill that he said is student- and sponsors’friendly. According to him, “NELFUND is like manna from heaven; that is the way I would describe it. It is one of the most significant public policy initiatives ever introduced into this country since independence. I have to commend President Ahmed Tinubu for what he has done. He signed the NELFUND bill. There was an initial version which was developed during the time of President Buhari, but it was never signed into law. To the credit of President Tinubu, he signed the first one into law, and then when he saw that there were some operational defects, he decided to repeal and then approach the parliament to enact a new one early 2024.” Professor Omoregie, who said he was part of the technical crew involved in the review of that initial one, said there was a lot of pruning down to accommodate some of the fears of the former president that it almost totally diluted its core value. “They were talking about guarantees that people had to guarantee when they took the facility. They even limited the amount that was to be drawn to a certain amount; there was nothing like upkeep of all of those things. President Tinubu didn’t think it was good enough, and he had to bring a new version. “I am sure even from outside the country now they will come and study sooner rather than later because, unlike many of the student loans that you have in America, the UK and all that, which makes them sceptical, this one is an interest-free loan. Maybe they should even use another word instead of calling it a loan. This is more like a grant; there is a moratorium that until you start working, nobody is going to bother you, and when you start working, nobody is going to ask you to pay with the bulk; rather, they would just take just a minute portion of your emolument. Everything will work out in such a way that you will not be burning out.” The post Nigeria’s NELFUND better than US, UK education loan models – UNIBEN VC appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Invest In Training, Boost Production To 3m/b Per Day, PETAN Urges Indigenous Oil Firms
item.description: The Petroleum Technology Association of Nigeria (PETAN) has urged indigenous oil and gas companies to invest in training young Nigerians and strengthening technical capacity to support the country’s ambition of producing three million barrels of crude oil per day. PETAN Chairman, Wole Ogunsanya, made the call at the association’s media roundtable in Lagos on Monday, warning that the transfer of oil and gas assets from international oil companies to indigenous operators had created an urgent need to train the next generation of industry professionals. He said Nigeria faced a widening gap between experienced oil and gas workers and younger professionals entering the industry, stressing that local operators must develop training programmes to sustain production and retain technical expertise. “We have a huge gap between those that are experienced in the industry versus age. Training is a very important aspect of our industry,” Ogunsanya said. PETAN Chairman, Wole Ogunsanya, while addressing journalists at a media roundtable in Lagos on Monday, October 26, 2026. He noted that many experienced Nigerian professionals had received their training through multinational companies, including Shell, ExxonMobil, Chevron and TotalEnergies, often benefiting from international placements and technical development programmes. However, he questioned whether similar opportunities would remain available as international operators divested some of their onshore, swamp and shallow-water assets. “Now we are divesting the assets. We are selling the assets to indigenous companies. Almost 100 per cent of the assets on land, in the swamp and shallow waters are owned by Nigerian indigenous companies. “Who is going to train the Nigerians? The new generation of Nigerians are coming behind to take over and operate those assets and work for these companies successfully,” he said. Training Centre Ogunsanya said Nigeria had sufficient human resources to develop its oil and gas industry, but needed to do more to attract graduates and provide them with practical skills. “The issue is not that we don’t have Nigerian young educated graduates that can come into the industry. The issue is how do we encourage these young educated Nigerian graduates to look into the oil and gas industry?” he asked. He said the industry required professionals with practical experience in drilling, pipeline installation, fabrication, welding and offshore operations, adding that training must prepare young Nigerians for the physical and technical demands of the sector. Ogunsanya disclosed that PETAN recruited nearly 100 engineers every two years through its internship programme, placing them in member companies for practical training. “After two years, PETAN members absorb over 60 per cent of these guys because that’s how good the training that we’re giving them is,” he said. item.title: Nigeria needs 9% annual growth to reduce poverty – Soludo
item.description: Governor Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra says Nigeria needs an annual economic growth of at least nine per cent to significantly reduce poverty and create jobs. He made the assertion at the Nigerian Economic Summit 32 (NES32) with the theme “Growth that Works: Delivering Jobs, Productivity and Shared Prosperity” in Abuja on Monday. He said that Nigeria’s current growth rate of about four per cent remained inadequate to achieve rapid poverty reduction and employment generation. The governor also said that Nigeria would require an annual growth of at least 12 per cent to achieve a one-trillion-dollar economy by 2030 or 2040. He added that the country’s investment rate, estimated at 17 to 20 per cent, must rise significantly to support the required economic expansion. Soludo cautioned against being misled by large nominal spending figures, saying that consolidated public expenditure across all government levels amounted to less than one dollar per person daily. He stressed the need to channel national savings into productive investments, capable of expanding economic output, creating jobs and improving living standards. He called for stronger coordination between the federal government, states and local governments, noting that subnational authorities accounted for a substantial share of public spending. According to him, effective collaboration is essential to maximise the impact of government policies and investments across the country. Soludo cited Anambra’s free education programme, which covers kindergarten through secondary school, as an example of interventions delivering measurable social benefits. He said that the state had reduced its out-of-school children rate from 2.5 per cent to 0.25 per cent. He also cited a recent Oxford and United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) report which reportedly placed Anambra’s multidimensional poverty rate at 9.6 per cent. Soludo said that reducing food prices required structural reforms to address post-harvest losses, which he put at about 43 per cent of agricultural output. He said that improving storage, transportation and distribution systems would help to move food from farms to urban markets and reduce consumer prices. The governor, therefore, urged governments to strengthen sectoral collaboration and mobilise investments to accelerate economic growth. Soludo also called for policies that encourage exports, develop domestic value chains and promote investment in sectors where Nigeria has competitive advantages. He emphasised that stronger private-sector participation and productive investments were essential to generating sustainable jobs and ensuring that economic growth benefitted more Nigerians. ( NAN ) The post Nigeria needs 9% annual growth to reduce poverty – Soludo appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Northern leaders must share blame for region’s backwardness – Gov Uba Sani
item.description: Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, has said political office holders in Northern Nigeria since 1999 must accept responsibility for the region’s developmental challenges, including its high number of out-of-school children. Sani made the remarks while defending President Bola Tinubu’s record in office, arguing that Northern leaders should not blame the current administration alone for problems that have persisted for decades. “I’m a northerner, and I’m telling you that anybody who held position, whether a governor, minister, senator, vice president, you should be ready to take blame,” he said. The governor cited figures on out-of-school children, stating that Nigeria had about 18 million children out of school as of 2023, with approximately 70 per cent living in Northern Nigeria. He questioned whether Tinubu, who assumed office in May 2023, should be held solely responsible for a crisis that predates his administration. Sani also disclosed that Kaduna State had about 550,000 out-of-school children when he assumed office in 2023, claiming that his administration had returned 300,000 of them to classrooms. He urged political leaders to move away from regional sentiments in their campaigns, insisting that voters should assess candidates based on their records in public office rather than their geographical origins. “The people of Northern Nigeria are very smart. You cannot come to them and tell them, ‘Vote for me because I’m a northerner.’ They will never vote for you. They can only vote for you based on your track record,” he said. The governor also highlighted federal road projects in the North-East and North-West as evidence of infrastructure development under Tinubu. According to him, more than 348 kilometres of roads had been completed in the North-East, while about 3,100 kilometres were under construction. He added that approximately 1,800 kilometres of the ongoing projects were nearing 90 per cent completion. In the North-West, Sani said more than 342 kilometres of roads had been completed, while another 1,042 kilometres were nearing 90 per cent completion. On education financing, the governor said more than 414,000 students from the North-West had benefited from the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), with about N84 billion allocated to the region. He described the student loan scheme as an intervention for young people from low-income households who might otherwise struggle to finance their education. Sani further stressed the importance of technical and vocational education and training (TVET), saying skills development was essential to addressing unemployment and expanding opportunities for young people in Northern Nigeria. He maintained that education remained critical to the region’s development and urged political leaders to focus on policies and programmes that improve the lives of residents. item.title: Nigeria’s Index Ebola Patient, Husband Evacuated To Switzerland – Pate
item.description: Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Ali Pate, on Monday confirmed that the first imported Ebola virus disease case in the country has been flown out of the country to Switzerland. Pate made the confirmation on his X handle, stating that the index patient, who has clinically improved, is stable and conscious, was evacuated along with her husband, who remained asymptomatic. He wrote: “I confirm that, with my approval, earlier this morning, the index case for Nigeria’s first imported Ebola virus disease departed Abuja for Switzerland. The index patient was clinically much improved, stable, conscious, communicating, and her clinical laboratory test results closing towards baseline. He, however, stated that her improvements do not mean she is not infectious, stating that strict protocols were put in place before her evacuation. “This does not mean she is not still infectious, hence the strict protocols in place. The patient was evacuated along with her spouse who has remained asymptomatic. ‘I thank all the various clinical staff for the high quality care they provided the patient as well as the public health personnel who ensured the evacuation was carried out in line with best public health measures for such evacuations. “We will provide further updates later this afternoon after the patient and her spouse lands successfully in their destination. “All public health measures are continuing to ensure successful containment of the imported virus. “I urge Nigerians to remain vigilant and rely on information from credible sources”, Pate said. The development came after the Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), on Sunday, said that the number of contacts linked to the index case of Ebola recorded in October 2026 had risen to 53. The agency said the contacts comprise health workers as well as the domestic staff and spouse of the patient diagnosed with the disease. The NCDC, in its Ebola Disease Situation Report, said that a newly suspected case was reported by Rivers State on October 23, but laboratory results returned negative for Ebola disease. “Fifty-three contacts linked to the index case have so far been identified, categorized and followed up. Contacts listed include healthcare workers, domestic staff and spouse,” the report dated October 24, 2026, partly read. Giving a background on the index case, it said the patient is a 42-year-old woman who returned from Uganda through Addis Ababa on October 3, 2026, via an international flight to Abuja, Nigeria. The agency said she became symptomatic four days later and presented to a private health facility on October 10, and another on October 11. “She presented to another private facility on the 11th of October 2026, where she was admitted. item.title: Delta: Police arrest school bus driver over alleged kidnap, assault of 14-year-old
item.description: By Emmauel Okogba The Delta State Police Command has arrested a 28-year-old school bus driver, Onome Lucky Ughagha, over the alleged kidnapping and sexual assault of a 14-year-old female student in Sapele. The suspect was also accused of demanding and collecting ₦503,000 from the victim’s father as ransom before abandoning the girl along Oton Road, Sapele. The police said the incident was reported at the Sapele Area Command on October 20, 2026, by the victim’s father, who alleged that the suspect abducted his daughter while she was preparing to leave for school. According to a statement by the Police Public Relations Officer, Delta State Command, SP Bright Edafe, the suspect allegedly contacted the girl’s father, demanded ₦503,000 and threatened to kill the minor if the money was not paid. The statement said the victim was abandoned along Oton Road after the ransom was paid and subsequently reunited with her family in a traumatised condition, with indications that she had been sexually assaulted. Following the report, operatives of the Sapele Area Command commenced investigations, while the victim was taken to a medical facility for examination and treatment. The police added that the school principal and vice principal were invited for questioning as efforts intensified to apprehend the suspect, who had allegedly abandoned the school bus and fled. Edafe said the suspect was eventually arrested on October 23 at his hideout in the Ajimele area of Sapele following intelligence-led operations. “During preliminary interrogation, he reportedly confessed to his involvement in the crime,” the statement said. The police disclosed that arrangements were underway to transfer the suspect to the State Criminal Investigation Department in Asaba for further investigation. The Commissioner of Police in Delta State, CP Samuel Erale, condemned the incident and reaffirmed the command’s commitment to protecting children from violence and exploitation. He assured that the investigation would be thorough and that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The commissioner also urged school authorities, parents and transport operators to strengthen measures to protect children, stressing that the safety of every child entrusted to their care must remain a priority. item.title: Ondo Assembly passes bill for establishment of state police
item.description: Ondo State House of Assembly has passed a bill seeking to amend the 1999 Constitution to provide for the establishment of state police services. The bill was passed following deliberations by the lawmakers at a plenary session on Monday in Akure. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the proposal was conveyed to the assembly in a letter from the National Assembly Clerk, Kamoru Ogunlana, which was read by the Speaker, Olamide Oladiji, on Sept. 24. The House Leader, Olatunji Oshati, who moved for the passage and its transmission to the National Assembly, said the lawmakers had considered the implications of the proposed amendment for the citizenry. Oshati said that the establishment of state police would address the numerous security challenges confronting the country. The motion was seconded by Mr Allen Oluwatoyin, All Progressives Congress (APC), member representing Ese-Odo State Constituency. Also speaking, Oladiji described the proposed establishment of state police as long overdue, saying it would enable security agencies to respond more swiftly to crime and other security concerns. He noted that state policing, being grassroots-based, would reduce crime through improved intelligence gathering and proactive security measures. “There will be greater confidence in state policing. It will strengthen intelligence gathering and provide grassroots security,” he added. The speaker, however, commended the lawmakers for their contributions to the bill and its passage. It was gathered that the bill would be transmitted to the National Assembly for further legislative consideration. (NAN) The post Ondo Assembly passes bill for establishment of state police appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Video: Pastor marries 2nd wife, says ‘monogamy is unbiblical’
item.description: Pastor Israel Ford of LifeWorks Church in Wickliffe, Ohio, United States, has announced his marriage to a second wife, describing monogamy as unbiblical. In a post on Facebook, Pastor Ford supported his action with Exodus 21:10. The Bible reference says: “If he take him another wife; her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage, shall he not diminish” (King James Version). A video accompanying the post has first wife, Prophetess Lydia Ford, introducing Minister Shakayla Ford as her husband’s second wife. She said they had been privately married for three years. Pastor Ford wrote: “I would like to introduce to the world, my second wife, Shakayla Ford. “As a nation, we have been taught that a man should have one wife only. This is unbiblical. “I encourage you to watch today’s sermon in its entirety. I understand that this is an unpopular truth that we have gotten away from and many Pastors will not preach. “I have no plans to choose pleasing man over what God has revealed. item.title: Man Utd crisis deepens as Carrick faces axe
item.description: Winless in eight games and hovering just above the Premier League relegation zone, struggling Manchester United are facing the prospect of yet another managerial change, with Michael Carrick likely to pay the price. The former United midfielder was warmly applauded by fans as he made his way down the tunnel after his team’s chastening 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday. Moments later a chorus of boos erupted as the players left the pitch — with fans clear in their minds where the blame lies for United’s current malaise. Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after inspiring an impressive revival following the team’s struggles under Ruben Amorim — United secured third place in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League. But a drastic decline this season is an all-too-familiar story for United supporters, who last witnessed a Premier League title triumph 13 years ago under Alex Ferguson. An emotional Carrick denied his lap of the pitch at full-time on Sunday was a goodbye as he struggles to come to terms with his team’s precipitous decline. “I definitely knew that we hadn’t cracked it and there was a lot of work to be done, but that doesn’t mean to say that it should have gone this way,” he said. Carrick, 45, is clinging on but his position appears increasingly precarious, with former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann apparently in the frame for the job. The United boss, who won multiple titles in the club’s golden era under Ferguson, was the seventh permanent appointment since the Scot retired. David Moyes was proven in the Premier League, Louis van Gaal and Jose Mourinho had stellar records and Erik ten Hag and Amorim were seen as rising stars of coaching. – Sentimental choice – Carrick is in the same category as Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, who was in charge for three years from 2018 — a sentimental choice as a former player who played a major role in the club’s glory years under Ferguson. “The Manchester United fans are singing the Michael Carrick song because I think they know what’s going to happen here. They’ve seen this before. He’s one of their own and he’s popular,” former United captain Gary Neville told Sky Sports. “But the owners, the sporting department and the players are not popular and they’ve badly let this football club down.” The problems at the club, as Neville points out, go far beyond the dugout. Despite fierce, ongoing protests from fans, the US-based Glazer family still hold a majority stake in the club Malcolm Glazer bought via a leveraged takeover in 2005, saddling United with huge debts. Any hopes that the arrival of British billionaire Jim Ratcliffe as a minority owner in 2024 would signal a new dawn have been dashed. Ratcliffe has overseen cost-cutting measures including widespread redundancies and ticket hikes but the club’s debt has still soared above £1.1 billion ($1.47 billion). item.title: US singer Chris Brown avoids jail over UK nightclub brawl
item.description: American R&B singer Chris Brown avoided jail when sentenced by a UK court Monday after pleading guilty to a public order offence during a 2023 brawl at a London nightclub. The former boyfriend of music sensation Rihanna was handed an eight-month jail sentence suspended for a year — meaning he will not be imprisoned unless he commits another offence during the period. Brown, 37, who was wearing a black face mask and black cap when he arrived Monday at Southwark Crown Court in London, had admitted to affray during an appearance in July. “Violence of this kind in a crowded nightclub is serious. It creates an obvious risk, not merely to the person against whom it is directed, but also to others,” judge Tony Baumgartner said, handing down the sentence. Prosecutors had accused him and co-defendant Omololu Akinlolu, also a US national, of carrying out “a vicious and unprovoked attack” in a crowded nightclub “where Brown used a glass bottle as a weapon to strike the victim’s head twice”. The guilty plea avoided a trial on several other charges, including attempting to cause grievous bodily harm with intent and possession of an offensive weapon, namely a bottle. Brown, who has sold tens of millions of records worldwide, had earlier denied those charges. All of the allegations relate to an incident at Tape, a private members’ club in central London, on February 19, 2023, while Brown was touring the UK. The victim was struck several times with a bottle before being pursued, punched and kicked. The singer is known for mid-2000s hits such as “Kiss, Kiss”, as well as a litany of legal troubles including a felony conviction for assaulting Rihanna in 2009. Brown rose from a local church choir in Virginia to sudden fame with his rich R&B voice before turning to rap. He was convicted of having beaten then-girlfriend Rihanna before the 2009 Grammy Awards, forcing the pop star to miss the annual gala. In 2012, Brown was involved in an altercation at a New York nightclub with members of hip hop star Drake’s entourage, during which French basketball player Tony Parker suffered an eye injury after being hit by a thrown glass bottle. Two years later, Brown pleaded guilty to assaulting a fan in Washington. Akinlolu, 40 also pleaded guilty to affray over the London incident. He was sentenced to four months’ imprisonment suspended for a year. The post US singer Chris Brown avoids jail over UK nightclub brawl appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Peter Obi demands supporter’s release, accuses Tinubu of undermining democracy
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi has demanded the release of party supporter Rilwan Olawale, accusing President Bola Tinubu of undermining democracy by “encouraging and facilitating violence.” In a statement posted on X on Monday, Obi described the reported incident as part of what he called the intimidation and harassment of his supporters. He also accused President Bola Tinubu of encouraging and facilitating violence, and demanded transparency over Olawale’s reported arrest, respect for his rights and an end to what he described as politically motivated harassment. “The continued intimidation and harassment of my supporters across the country, the latest being the case of Rilwan Olawale, is disturbing and unacceptable. “President Bola Tinubu has remained a huge beneficiary of our democracy and should not brazenly be destroying it by encouraging and facilitating violence.” Obi further stated that his campaign was peaceful and issue-driven, and warned that his supporters’ restraint should not be mistaken for weakness. “We have chosen the path of peace, not violence; persuasion, not intimidation. However, nobody should mistake our civility for weakness, our restraint for fear, or our commitment to peace for an absence of resolve. We will not be intimidated into silence, nor will we abandon Nigerians who believe in a New Nigeria that is possible and will be OK.” He called for Olawale’s release and said Nigerians should be free to support the candidate of their choice. “I therefore demand transparency regarding Rilwan Olawale’s arrest, his release, respect for his rights, and an end to politically motivated harassment. No government or political party has the right to deny Nigerians the freedom to support a candidate of their choice. “We will remain peaceful but resolute. We will not resort to violence, but we will stand firmly and lawfully against every attempt to undermine our democratic rights.” According to NDC’s Lagos governorship candidate, Funso Doherty, Olawale was reportedly taken from his residence at about 1 a.m. on Sunday by men who identified themselves as Department of State Services (DSS) operatives. Doherty, in a statement on his X handle on Sunday, said he was in contact with Olawale’s family and legal counsel, who were seeking to establish what happened and gain access to him. He said: “This afternoon, reports reached me that Mr. Rilwan Olawale, a strong NDC supporter, who is also identified with the Obidient movement, was allegedly picked up by some armed men who identified themselves as operatives of the Department of State Services in the very early hours of today, Sunday 25th October.” Doherty also urged the public to remain calm while the family and legal counsel sought information about Olawale’s whereabouts. item.title: Trump blasts Norway over Nobel Peace Prize snub
item.description: US President Donald Trump attacked Norway during a campaign rally, calling it a “shit house country,” and said that Norwegian immigrants were not welcome in the United States because its Nobel Committee had not awarded him the Peace Prize. “Frankly, Norway sucks. Norway has become a shit house country, actually,” he said during Sunday’s speech. Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has made no secret of his desire to win the prestigious Nobel Peace prize. Judge and former UN rights chief Navi Pillay of South Africa was this year’s recipient of the prize. Trump has called the committee’s choice “a disgraceful and embarrassing decision” and argued that the award should have gone to him. Trump said Sunday he would welcome immigrants from certain countries but not Norway “because I didn’t get the Nobel Prize.” “So I don’t want anybody from Norway,” he said during the rally in the Michigan town of Port Huron ahead of crucial US midterm elections on November 3. There was no official indication of a new US policy on Norwegian immigrants. Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide responded to Trump’s comments about the Nobel prize on Monday, maintaining that the committee is independent. “He knows very well that the Nobel Committee is independent. We have reminded him of that, in case anyone is wondering – and that is still the case,” he told national broadcaster NRK. Trump came under fire in 2018, during his first term, after using similar vulgar expressions to refer to Haiti and certain African countries. item.title: Ebola: Yobe Govt Activates Emergency Response Centres, Border Surveillance
item.description: The Yobe State government said it has not yet recorded any Ebola virus but has activated its Public Health Emergency Incident Management System and developed a comprehensive Emergency Preparedness and Response plan to monitor the possible outbreak of the disease. The Commissioner for Health, Dr. Mohammed Lawan Gana, represented by the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry, Hadiza Sabo, disclosed this while briefing journalists in Damaturu on Monday. According to her, the state government is building 6 technical pillars recommended by the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control for the Ebola Virus Disease response, which are coordinated through the Emergency Operations Centre (EOC). “Yobe State shares an international border; consequently, the state is strengthening cross-border surveillance and coordination with transport and relevant border authorities at key entry points to enhance vigilance, facilitate the timely detection and reporting of public health threats, and support prompt response to potential disease outbreaks” “We have outlined six pillars of coordination and management: epidemiology and surveillance, case management, infection prevention and control, laboratory services, communication and community engagement, as well as point of entry,” she said. Sabo further added that the government is intensifying public awareness campaigns using radio, television, community town carriers and engagement with traditional leaders. “Our message is simple; Ebola is real, but it is preventable and controllable. We are advising citizens to maintain good hand hygiene, avoid direct contact with the bodily fluids of anyone showing symptoms, and report any unusual illness or death to the nearest health facility immediately”. The government advises the general public to shun any rumours or misinformation and rely on verified information from the State Ministry of Health, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) and other official sources, and not to spread unverified reports on social media, as doing that can cause unnecessary panic and harm.
